the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher writes or reads “Presents views appreciating the importance of public services of the times” and asks students to name one example they have seen in everyday life. Students share brief responses; the teacher connects their examples to Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency 8.1.1 and explains how it will help them explore this period's outcome.

post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Each student completes a short exit response explaining one finding about “Presents views appreciating the importance of public services of the times” using evidence or an example from Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency 8.1.1. The teacher reviews responses for an accurate link to the period outcome.
selected_activity:
Activity: Citizen-Officer Deliberation Roleplay: Competency 8.1.1
Approach: Students use citizen-officer deliberation roleplay to explore 'Presents views appreciating the importance of public services of the times.'. Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (35 students): Desks arranged into 7 teams (7 teams (7 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (35 students): Desks arranged into 7 teams (7 teams (7 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 35 students using 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 7 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: A short role-based civic decision and its reasons.
Grouping: 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
